findings.claim: Window-share is not a portable denominator: it is plan-specific (subscription 5h/weekly vs pay-per-token GLM), nonlinear within a window (n=30: 30->65% for 260k tokens), polluted by other consumers on the same account (n=33: 8->72% with no local runs), and invisible to z.ai; scoring tiers per window-share cannot compare Astra against GLM or Sonnet-max against Opus-max users.

State log records nonlinear jumps, other-consumer pollution, and budget-stop events that confirm the denominator moves without local runs.

findings.remedy: Score with a vector, not one denominator: tokens in/out+cached, wall time, and window-share where defined, plus money where billable; normalize usefulness per 1M input tokens as the cross-vendor comparator and keep window-share as a routing constraint, not the score.
findings.trigger: Comparing an Astra high round (10-15% of 5h window) against a GLM max round (no window, money cost) or across users on different plans.
findings.verification: Recompute the nine accepted rounds F46-1..F62-1 in both units (window-% vs tokens) and check whether the ranking of tiers flips.

With only sent-tier logged, GLM high mixes requested-medium and requested-high; no field records endpoint caps version or raw model string.

findings.claim: The proposed worker event still leaks task shape: duration/token/tool/edit/verification buckets plus agent id and timing joinable to ledger consult_refs fingerprint task size and workflow, and the old agent_report free-text event is one misroute away from breaking the closed-class contract.

findings.remedy: MUST stay out: prompts, paths, names, transcript excerpts, task_scope text, raw token counts, session/transcript paths; coarse-bucket counts only, agent id as a one-way pseudonym rotated per task, explicit blocklist test rejecting free-text fields at intake.

findings.claim: Scout-and-judge without a falsification budget will hide defects: a cheap scout optimizes for plausible digests, the judge anchored on the digest under-checks omitted hunks, and a stale digest surviving a cold cache silently narrows the judge's scope; no output cap alone keeps the judge honest.

evidence.observation: Routing proposes a cheap tier writing a digest handoff consumed by the judge plus a call cap, with the digest surviving a cold cache.
Quota history shows cold-cache pressure is real (96% fork cost, 8-23% per round), so digest staleness and scope-narrowing are the likely failure mode, not cost.

findings.remedy: Require the scout to emit diff-range coverage (files+hunk counts) plus verbatim suspicious hunks under a byte cap, and require the judge to re-read at least one unmentioned hunk and report coverage; measure miss rate on seeded-defect calibration diffs.
findings.trigger: A defect in a hunk the scout summarized as clean and excluded from the digest.
findings.verification: Seed one defect outside the digest on a test diff and check the judge still finds it under the cap.

reply_markdown:
Framing challenge: the brief asks how to measure tiers, but the decision that locks in value is routing under scarcity, not scoring after months. Both sketches assume one closed table can serve billing, privacy, and learning; those goals conflict. Decide the routing policy first (what the bridge does when the window is hot), then derive the minimal telemetry that can falsify it.

**Q1. Tiers and denominator.** Do not assign fixed tiers per purpose yet; assign a default plus an exploration budget (e.g. 10% of reviews run one tier lower/higher). Unlisted designs: (a) calibration set — rerun a frozen defect-seeded diff monthly at each tier; (b) token-denominated cost as the cross-vendor score, window-share only as a same-account constraint; (c) usefulness per confirmed finding, not per mark. To choose I need: purpose mix shares, GLM price vs subscription shadow price, and whether z.ai tiers are speed- or quality-ordered (finding #2).

**Q2. Worker capture.** SubagentStop alone is the wrong point; use Start (intent: tier, effort, task class) joined by agent id to Stop (outcome, usage) plus a coordinator rework flag (used-as-is | reworked | discarded). Keep out everything in finding #4. Attribution: credit = worker outcome class × coordinator disposition, never a single usefulness bit. To choose I need: five real hook stdin samples and the Codex/Kimi equivalent signal.

**Q3. Schema.** Add now or break later: `effort_requested`, `effort_sent`, `caps_version`, `purpose`, `task_class` (review/worker shared enum), `disposition` (rework flag), `judge_source`, and a `schema_version` + reserved `other` on every new enum. Keep consult and worker events disjoint; never extend `agent_report`.

**Q4. Scout-and-judge.** It fails exactly where quotas bite: the scout drops the hunk containing the defect and the judge, call-capped and anchored, never re-opens it. A byte cap is insufficient; require coverage attestation (hunk list + omitted ranges) plus one mandatory judge re-read outside the digest (finding #5). To choose I need: the miss rate on seeded diffs at scout-low vs scout-medium.

## Requested checks
RC1 (read-only): `cat` five real `SubagentStop` hook stdin payloads from `~/.claude/hooks/` session logs — settles finding #3 effort visibility. Budget: 30 min.
RC2 (read-only): run the same brief at z.ai requested `medium` vs `high`, diff sent tier in ledger `effort_sent` — settles tier collapse. Budget: 2 consults.
unproven: Whether z.ai glm-5.3 exposes more than three effective tiers or silently remaps them.
Whether coordinator usefulness marks correlate with findings-confirmed hits once the findings join exists.
Whether a weekly optimiser note changes tier choice versus a static recommendation table.
verdict_reason: Framing needs a routing-first redesign with a portable cost vector and Start/Stop worker join before any closed-schema freeze.
